title: Machine Learning Foundations
audience: First-year university STEM students learning introductory machine learning.
educator_goal: Give students grounded help between office hours while keeping teachers informed about confusion hotspots.

topics.title: What supervised learning is
topics.summary: Supervised learning fits a mapping from labeled examples to predictions. It is the foundation for both regression and classification tasks.
objectives: Explain the difference between input features and target labels.
Describe why labeled examples are necessary in supervised learning.

materials.excerpt: In supervised learning, each training example contains input features and a target label. The model learns a mapping from inputs to outputs by comparing predictions against known answers.
Classification predicts a category such as spam or not spam, while regression predicts a continuous value such as house price. Both are standard supervised learning tasks.

topics.title: Why training, validation, and test splits matter
topics.summary: Data splits separate model fitting from model selection and final evaluation. Without clean splits, performance estimates become misleading.
objectives: Explain the job of the training split.
Explain why the validation split is used during development.
Explain why the test split should stay untouched until the end.

materials.excerpt: The training split is used to fit model parameters. The validation split supports model choice and hyperparameter tuning, and the test split is reserved for the final unbiased estimate of performance.
If the test data influences model decisions during development, the final score becomes optimistic because the model has effectively seen the answers already.

topics.title: Overfitting and generalization
topics.summary: A model can memorize noise from the training set and fail on new examples. Generalization means performing well on data that was not seen during training.
objectives: Explain why strong training performance alone is not enough.
Connect model complexity with generalization risk.

materials.excerpt: Overfitting occurs when a model captures accidental patterns in the training data instead of learning the underlying signal. Such a model looks strong during training but performs poorly on fresh examples.
Generalization is the ability to keep useful performance on unseen data. Validation and test results matter because they reveal whether the learned pattern transfers beyond the training set.
